rationale: A defensible downside-quality reframing of the archive's restated-profitability ratio, but it is the same construct with MA(·,3) swapped for TS_MIN(·,5) and will be very highly correlated with IntangibleCapitalizedProfitability, so the incremental information content is likely thin and it risks being scored as an operator-level variant rather than a new mechanism.

This is SustainedResearchFloorCashBacked with oancf replaced by ib+dp — a proxy substitution that the reasoning itself frames as a coverage diagnostic, and since ib+dp is near-collinear with operating cash flow at annual frequency it is a cosmetic variant of an already-evaluated signal rather than a substantively different hypothesis.

TS_MIN(xrd/at,5) is empirically almost the same variable as xrd/at, so this is effectively a near-duplicate of the archive's InnovatorLowRolloverBurden, and the short-term-debt leg is a well-known low-leverage/distress sort providing little incremental mechanism beyond a mechanical leg swap between two existing signals.

Broadening the validation denominator from acquired to total (acquired plus internally accumulated) intangible capital is an economically coherent generalization that should roughly double breadth on the archive's best-balanced ratio, though the denominator collapses toward zero for low-intangible firms and the winsorized rank should be checked for whether it degenerates into a plain cash-flow-to-capital profitability sort.

The sign logic is internally consistent (deep loss trough plus a heavy intangible book predicts low returns) and the impairment-trigger framing is more specific than the earlier coverage leg, but the trough-earnings leg is largely the well-documented loss-firm/profitability effect, so the signal must be shown to add something beyond a distress sort interacted with intangible intensity.

The within-firm peak-normalized research intensity is a genuinely different, scale-free retrenchment measure that the archive has not tested and is not simply another cross-sectional level sort, though it partially overlaps the known R&D-change literature, will be undefined/zero for firms without R&D, and may have little dispersion since most continuous spenders sit near their own five-year max.
